mainTopic: How far back stains and a שרץ make things impure, which found stains are pure, and when the כותים are believed
overview: The amud first finishes a question about how far back impurity reaches. A שרץ found in a מבוי, or a כתם found on a garment, makes things impure only back to the last sweeping or laundering. The גמרא asks whether that is because the person surely checked at that time, or because the cleaning itself would have removed the problem. From רבי מאיר's ברייתא it concludes that sweeping and laundering count because a check is presumed (חזקתו בדוק). רבי אחא and רבי then give ways to tell whether a stain came before or after a laundering. רבי אלעזר explains that רבי שמעון's leniency for a moist item applies only to a שרץ, because a moist כתם might be an old stain that got wet. A new משנה then rules on stains coming from רקם, from גוים, and from places with ישראל and כותים. The גמרא uses that משנה to discuss accepting converts from תרמוד and rereads the dispute about the כותים. A final משנה teaches that stains found lying anywhere are pure, with two exceptions. It also covers the כותים's בית הטמאות and lists what the כותים are and are not believed about. It closes with the rule that they are not believed about any matter they are suspected of not keeping.

steps.title: A second difference for the alley: the שרץ was found in a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another practical difference between 'examined' and 'swept' for the מבוי: a case where the שרץ was found inside a hole in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the difference shows up when the שרץ was found in a hole. If the presumption is 'examined,' then whoever checks the alley also checks the holes. If the presumption is 'swept,' sweeping does not reach into a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving a second answer to 'what is the practical difference' between the two ways of understanding the swept alley. This time the case is a שרץ found in a hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sweeping means the alley was carefully checked, the checker would have looked in the hole too. So the שרץ must have arrived later, and earlier טהרות stay pure. If sweeping only means the ground was cleaned, a hole was never cleaned. The שרץ may have been there all along, so even earlier טהרות are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; introduces another possible answer
Its presumed status
Examined, checked
Swept clean
A hole or pit in the ground

phrases.english: Alternatively, where it was found in a hole,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שרץ found in the alley, from the case the גמרא was just discussing.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference also appears when the שרץ is found in a hole: checking covers holes, sweeping does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Checking reaches hidden spots, but cleaning only reaches the open surface.

steps.title: The same question about laundering a stained garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the כתם part of the משנה and asks: does laundering work because the garment was surely checked, or because laundering would wash out any stain?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says, 'And likewise the stain, etc.' The question was asked: when the משנה says 'until the time of laundering,' is that because the garment is presumed to have been checked, or because it is presumed to have been washed clean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the כתם line of the משנה and asks the same kind of question it asked about the alley, now about a laundered garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a כתם makes a woman impure retroactively back to the time of laundering. The question is what laundering proves. One possibility is that whoever launders checks the garment carefully. The other is that the washing itself removes any stain that was there.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a woman's garment
A question was raised (an open question the גמרא tries to explore)
Laundering
Washed clean
Or perhaps

phrases.english: And likewise the stain, etc.
A question was raised before them:
'until the time of laundering':
is its presumption that it was examined,
or perhaps its presumption is that it was washed clean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question it asked about the alley to the garment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether laundering works because the garment was surely checked or because the washing removes any stain.

steps.title: What difference would it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two ways of understanding laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why the question matters. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually both sides lead to the same result: the woman is impure only back to the laundering. The גמרא wants a case where the two views would actually give different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Practical difference; a case where the two views give different results

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in the previous step matters in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'examined' and 'washed clean' lead to different rulings.

steps.title: First difference: he laundered but did not check
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the launderer says he washed the garment but did not check it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is where he said: 'I laundered but I did not check.' If the presumption is 'checked,' this garment was not checked. If the presumption is 'washed clean,' this garment was washed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a case where the launderer openly says he did not check the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If laundering works because of checking, there is no presumption here, since he admits he did not check. If laundering works because washing removes stains, it still works, since he did wash it.

keyTerms.meaning: He laundered but did not examine
This one, here

phrases.english: Where he said: 'I laundered but did not examine.'
If you say its presumption is that it was examined,
this one was not examined;
if you say its presumption is that it was washed clean,
this one was washed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When he laundered without checking: under 'checked' there is no presumption; under 'washed clean' there is.

steps.title: Second difference: the stain was found on the side of the garment
steps.stepSummary: Another difference: the כתם was found on the side of the garment, where washing may not reach well but a checker would look.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the difference is where the stain was found on the side. If the presumption is 'checked,' whoever checks also checks the side. If the presumption is 'washed clean,' the side does not get washed clean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second practical difference for the garment, matching the 'hole' case it gave for the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If laundering means checking, the side was checked too. The stain must be new, and her earlier טהרות stay pure. If laundering only means washing, the side is not washed well enough to remove a stain. The stain may be old, so even items from before the laundering are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The side; the folded or seamed edge of a garment

phrases.english: Alternatively, where it was found on the side.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כתם, and 'the side' means the edges and folds of the garment.

phrases.english: If you say: 'its presumption is that it was examined,'
one who examines also examines the side.
If you say: 'its presumption is that it was washed clean,'
on the side it does not get washed clean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 3, matching the 'hole' case in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A stain on the side of the garment: checking covers it, washing does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The alley and the garment work the same way. There are two differences each time: 'cleaned but didn't check,' and 'found in a hidden spot' (a hole or the side of the garment).

steps.title: רבי מאיר: sweeping counts because people check while sweeping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is and brings רבי מאיר's ברייתא. It explains that a שרץ in a מבוי only makes things impure back to the last sweeping, because people are presumed to check their alleys when they sweep.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי מאיר said: Why did the חכמים say that a שרץ found in an alley makes things impure going backward only until the time someone can say 'I checked this alley and there was no שרץ in it,' or until the time it was swept? Because Jews are presumed to check their alleys when they sweep them. And if they did not check, they lose out going backward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the answer to its question and starts quoting a ברייתא from רבי מאיר about the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives the reason why sweeping works: Jews are presumed to check the alley while they sweep. So sweeping counts because it includes a check, not just because it cleans the alley. This is the first half of the proof, and the garment half follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Going backward in time (retroactively)
The time of sweeping
The presumption about; what we assume people normally do
They lost it, meaning the purity of their items

steps.title: רבי מאיר: laundering counts because women check while laundering
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר applies the same reasoning to a כתם on a garment. Women are presumed to check their garments when they launder them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they say that a stain found on a garment makes things impure going backward only until she can say 'I checked the garment and there was no stain on it,' or until the laundering? Because Jewish women are presumed to check their garments when they launder them. And if they did not check, they lose out going backward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר continues with the case of the stained garment, which is exactly the case the גמרא asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering protects the earlier items because women are presumed to check while laundering, not because the wash erases stains. That answers the question from step 2 directly. If she did not actually check, her items lose their purity going back.

steps.title: רבי אחא: wash it again to see when the stain came
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא gives a test for an unchecked garment: launder it again. If the stain fades, it came after the earlier wash. If it does not fade, it was there before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא said: Let her launder it again. If its look fades, we know the stain came after the laundering. If not, we know it came before the laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds רבי אחא's practical way to find out when a stain got onto a garment that was not checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stain that already went through one wash will not fade in another wash, but a fresh stain will. So a second wash shows whether the stain is older or newer than the first wash. This affects whether items she handled before that wash become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her launder it again
Its appearance faded or changed
It is known for sure

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha said: Let her launder it again.
If its appearance faded,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: it is known that it came after the laundering;
and if not, it is known that it came before the laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side addition in the ברייתא: how to date a stain on a garment that was not checked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wash the garment again. If the stain fades, it came after the first wash. If it does not fade, it came before.

steps.title: רבי: a stain's texture shows when it came
steps.stepSummary: רבי says there is no need to wash again. A stain from after laundering soaks into the cloth, while one from before laundering forms a crust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: A stain from after laundering does not look like a stain from before laundering. This one soaks in, and that one forms a crust.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different method from רבי אחא: just look at the stain itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a stain from after the wash and one from before it look different on the cloth. So you can tell their timing by looking, without doing a second laundering.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not similar
Soaks into the cloth
Forms a crust that sits on top

phrases.english: Rebbi says: It is not similar,
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: a stain from after the laundering
to a stain from before the laundering,
for this one soaks in and that one forms a crust.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the stain from after laundering, which soaks in. "That one" is the stain from before laundering, which forms a crust.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה כֶּתֶם שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַכִּבּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different method from רבי אחא's for dating the stain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tell the stain's timing by its texture: it soaks in if it came after laundering and forms a crust if it came before.

steps.title: Conclusion: swept or laundered means checked
steps.stepSummary: From רבי מאיר's words, the גמרא concludes that a swept alley or a laundered garment is presumed to have been checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: its presumption is that it was checked. Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question. Sweeping and laundering count because we assume a check was done at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason was 'people check while sweeping or laundering,' so the reason is the check and not the cleaning. That decides the practical cases from steps 4-5. For example, if the launderer says he washed but did not check, the laundering does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude from this
Its presumed status is 'checked'

steps.whatToRemember: Sweeping an alley or laundering a garment counts as a fresh starting point because it is presumed to include a check (חזקתו בדוק), not because the cleaning itself removes the problem.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think laundering works because water washes stains away. The גמרא concludes it works because she is assumed to have looked at the garment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical differences raised in steps 1 and 3-5, such as a launderer who washed but did not check, or a stain on the edge of the garment.

phrases.english: Learn from this: its presumption is that it was checked.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: חֶזְקָתוֹ בָּדוּק, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי מאיר's reason (steps 6-7) and draws the final answer to the question from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A swept alley or a laundered garment is presumed to have been checked, and that check is why it counts.

steps.title: A moist stain is still retroactive, even for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a moist or dry שרץ or כתם. רבי אלעזר says רבי שמעון's leniency for moist items applies only to a שרץ. A moist כתם is still retroactive, because it may have been dry and then gotten wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says it makes things impure whether it is moist or dry. רבי אלעזר says: they only taught this about a שרץ. But a moist stain also makes things impure going back, because we can say it was dry and water fell on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה. Then רבי אלעזר explains that רבי שמעון's leniency, which says a moist item does not reach back to the last check, applies only to a שרץ and not to a כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reasons that a moist item must be fresh, so it cannot reach far back in time. רבי אלעזר says this reasoning does not work for a כתם. A stain that looks moist now could be an old dry stain that recently got wet, so we still go back to the last laundering.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist, wet
Dry
Retroactively, going back in time
They only taught this about... (a phrase that limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Being moist sounds like a reason to be stricter, but here it is the lenient side. A moist item looks fresh, so it should not reach far back in time. רבי אלעזר says that for a כתם, being moist does not prove it is fresh.

phrases.english: And it renders impure whether moist, etc.
Rabbi Elazar said
They taught this only about a creeping animal
but a moist stain also

say it was dry
and water fell on it

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general rule that a swept alley and a laundered garment count as checked to the משנה's moist-versus-dry dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון's leniency for moist items applies only to a שרץ. A moist כתם still makes things impure back to the last laundering.

steps.title: Why not say the same about a moist creeping animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a moist שרץ could also have been dry and then gotten wet, so it should also be retroactive.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שרץ too: say it was dry and water fell on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. His own reasoning seems to work just as well for a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'maybe it was dry and water fell on it' is enough to make a moist כתם retroactive, the same argument should apply to a moist שרץ. Then רבי שמעון's leniency would have nothing left to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: A creeping animal too
say it was dry
and water fell on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרֶץ נָמֵי, אֵימַר יָבֵשׁ הָיָה וּמַיָּא נְפֻיל עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's distinction between a שרץ and a כתם.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's limiting of רבי שמעון's leniency to a שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'it was dry and got wet' argument seems to apply equally to a שרץ, so the distinction disappears.

steps.title: A dried creeping animal that got wet would fall apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if a dried-out שרץ had gotten wet, it would have broken apart. A whole, moist שרץ must be fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were really like that, it would have fallen apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A שרץ is different from a stain because a dried carcass that gets soaked does not look whole and moist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stain looks the same whether it was always moist or was dry and then got wet, so its moisture proves nothing. A dried-out dead animal that gets soaked breaks apart. If the שרץ is moist and whole, it really is fresh, and רבי שמעון's leniency applies.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were so
It would surely have fallen apart

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a moist שרץ is fresh and does not reach back, because a dried one that got wet would fall apart. A moist כתם still reaches back, because it may be an old stain that got wet.

phrases.english: If it were so that this is the case
it would surely have fallen apart

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אִיתָא דְּהָכִי הוּא — אִמַּרְטוּטֵי אִימַּרְטַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A moist שרץ could also be an old dry one that got wet.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dried שרץ that got wet would fall apart, so a whole, moist one must be fresh.

steps.title: New משנה: stains from רקם, from גוים, and from mixed places
steps.stepSummary: Stains from רקם are טהור, but רבי יהודה says they are טמא because the people there are misguided גרים. Stains from גוים are טהור. When stains come from a mix of ישראל and כותים, רבי מאיר says they are טמא and חכמים say they are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: All stains that come from רקם are pure. רבי יהודה says they are impure, because the people there are converts who are mistaken. Stains that come from among the gentiles are pure. For stains from among Jews and כותים, רבי מאיר says they are impure, and the חכמים say they are pure, because Jews are not suspected of leaving their stained garments around.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on stained garments that come from different groups of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stains of gentile women are טהור. So the question is who these garments probably belonged to. רבי יהודה treats the people of רקם as Jewish converts who are careless with their stained garments. In the mixed case, חכמים assume the stained garment did not come from a Jewish woman, because Jews put away their stained garments.

keyTerms.meaning: A town whose residents were mostly gentiles
Converts who are mistaken (careless with their stained garments)
Samaritans
They are not suspected

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stains from רקם and from גוים are טהור. For mixed Jewish and כותי sources, רבי מאיר rules טמא and חכמים rule טהור.

steps.title: The משנה makes no exception, so it includes תרמוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה rules that stains from גוים are טהור without any exception. That means it includes even תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה states it without exception: even from תרמוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the lesson רבי יוחנן will draw in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have made an exception for תרמוד, whose people might be suspected of being Jews of flawed lineage. Since it did not, the משנה seems to treat the people of תרמוד as real gentiles.

keyTerms.meaning: It states the rule without exception
A place with a gentile population; there was concern about whether its people were really of flawed Jewish lineage

phrases.english: GEMARA
It teaches the rule without exception
even from Tarmod!
phrases.notes: This refers to the line in the משנה that stains coming from among the gentiles are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה's wording about stains from גוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling that stains from גוים are טהור includes the people of תרמוד.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: converts may be accepted from תרמוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן concludes from the משנה that converts may be accepted from תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: this tells us that we accept converts from תרמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes the inference from the previous step and turns it into a practical rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stains of תרמוד's women count as gentile stains, then its people are treated as gentiles. That means they are not Jews of flawed lineage, so they may convert and join the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: This tells us (introduces a lesson learned from a source)
We accept converts

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rules that all stains from גוים are טהור, including those from תרמוד. From this, רבי יוחנן learns that the people of תרמוד count as gentiles and may be accepted as converts.
steps.whyThisMatters: A rule about purity is used to settle a question of lineage and conversion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said
This is to say
we accept converts from Tarmod

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the observation in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since the משנה treats people from תרמוד as gentiles, converts may be accepted from תרמוד.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said converts are not accepted from תרמוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 16: רבי יוחנן and the Elders both said converts are NOT accepted from תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יוחנן and the Elders both said that we do not accept converts from תרמוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what we just learned in step 16. רבי יוחנן supposedly said converts may be accepted from תרמוד, but there is a report that he said the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבי יוחנן learned from the משנה that converts from תרמוד are accepted. Here the גמרא brings a statement in which רבי יוחנן, together with the Elders, rules that they are not accepted. So רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge to what was just said
Converts
The Elders, a group of older sages
We do not accept

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rabbi Yochanan and the Elders,
who both say:
We do not accept converts from Tarmod!
phrases.notes: This is the exact opposite of what רבי יוחנן said in step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 16 with a contradicting statement of the same sage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 16 that converts are accepted from תרמוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רבי יוחנן is reported elsewhere, together with the Elders, as ruling that converts from תרמוד are not accepted.

steps.title: He cannot just be explaining the משנה without agreeing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: you cannot say רבי יוחנן only explained the משנה, because he holds the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי יוחנן only said 'this means' to explain the משנה, but he himself does not hold that way, that cannot be, because רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out of the contradiction and then immediately shoots it down. This makes the contradiction even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might answer that in step 16 רבי יוחנן was only reporting what the משנה implies, not his own view. But רבי יוחנן himself rules that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and our משנה is unnamed. So whatever the משנה implies should be his own ruling too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; the גמרא suggests a possible answer
This means; a way of drawing a lesson from a source
He does not hold that way himself
The הלכה follows an unnamed משנה, one with no sage's name on it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's real answer. The גמרא raises the answer only to reject it; the real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you would say,
"this" means, but he does not hold so,
phrases.notes: "זאת" points to רבי יוחנן's wording 'this means' in step 16, as if he were only explaining the משנה.

phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halakha follows an unattributed mishna!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא, זֹאת וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of step 17 by rejecting the obvious answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that רבי יוחנן in step 16 was only explaining the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, so what the unnamed משנה implies must also be his practical ruling.

steps.title: Later אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two statements come from different אמוראים who disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are different אמוראים, and they disagree about the opinion of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי יוחנן did not contradict himself; different later sages reported his view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One אמורא holds that רבי יוחנן said converts from תרמוד are not accepted, and so did not hold the rule about an unnamed משנה. Another אמורא holds that רבי יוחנן followed the unnamed משנה, so converts from תרמוד are accepted. The contradiction is between the reporters, not inside רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They are different אמוראים; two sages who disagree
According to the view of; about the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: Whether converts are accepted from תרמוד depends on which report of רבי יוחנן you follow. The two reports come from different אמוראים.

phrases.english: They are different amoraim,
and they disagree about Rabbi Yochanan's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 17-18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement among the people reporting the sage's view (אמוראי נינהו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to say both that converts from תרמוד are accepted and that they are not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruling is a different אמורא's report of רבי יוחנן's view, so רבי יוחנן did not contradict himself.

steps.title: Whose stains do the חכמים call impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about stains from among ישראל and כותים and asks: if the חכמים say ישראל stains are pure, whose stains are impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: stains from among ישראל and כותים. Now, the חכמים: if they call stains from ישראל pure, then whose stains do they call impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the next case in the משנה from step 14 and asks a question about the חכמים's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים say stains found among ישראל and כותים are טהור. The גמרא is puzzled by this. If even stains that may come from Jewish women are pure, it is unclear which stains the חכמים would ever call impure. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans; the group mixed with the ישראל in this case of the משנה
They declare pure
They declare impure
Etc.; the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: "From among Jews," etc.
And the Rabbis, if they deem those from Jews pure,
whose stains do they deem impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳. וְרַבָּנַן, אִי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְטַהֲרִי, דְּמַאן מְטַמּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרמוד discussion and returns to the next clause of the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to understand the חכמים's ruling of טהור for stains from among ישראל and כותים: if even stains that may come from ישראל are pure, which stains would they ever call impure?

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: the dispute is whether כותים are real converts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 20 by saying the משנה is incomplete. Stains from ישראל are impure for everyone. For stains from כותים, רבי מאיר says impure because they are true converts. The חכמים say pure because they converted only out of fear of lions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: stains from among Jews are impure. Stains from among the כותים: רבי מאיר says impure, because כותים are true converts. The חכמים say pure, because כותים are 'lion converts'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 20 by saying the משנה left out some words. It then fills them in: everyone agrees Jewish stains are impure, and the argument is only about stains of the כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, it looked like the חכמים call even Jewish stains pure, which made no sense. Now the 'pure' ruling of the חכמים is moved so it applies only to כותים. The reason for the disagreement is whether כותים count as Jews (גרי אמת) or as non-Jews (גרי אריות). The stains of non-Jews do not make things impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words; the גמרא fills in what is assumed
The people settled in שומרון whose status as Jews is debated
True converts, who count fully as Jews
'Lion converts', who converted out of fear of lions, so the conversion does not count
A blood stain found on a garment, which may carry impurity

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first attempt to rebuild the משנה. The גמרא will reject it in the next step and offer a different reading.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
From among Jews — impure,
from among the Samaritans — Rabbi Meir deems it impure,
because Samaritans are true converts,
and the Sages deem it pure,
because Samaritans are lion-converts.
phrases.notes: They converted only because lions were attacking them (מלכים ב 17), so the חכמים don't count it as a real conversion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by saying the משנה is missing words
steps.terutzResolutionType: Says the משנה is missing words (חסורי מחסרא) and fills them in
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to call even Jewish stains pure
steps.terutzMaskana: Jewish stains are impure for everyone; the dispute is only whether כותים are true converts

steps.title: The משנה's reason does not fit this reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the חכמים rule pure because כותים are lion converts, the משנה should give that as its reason. Instead it says 'because they are not suspected about their stains'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'because they are not suspected about their stains'? It should have said 'because they are lion converts'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 21. The reason the משנה actually gives does not match the reason that reading would need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21's version, the חכמים rule pure because כותים are not Jews. But the משנה's written reason talks about how careful people are with stained clothes. That is a completely different idea. A mismatched reason shows the rebuilt version cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if your reading is correct
Were suspected of something
It should have said

phrases.english: If so,
why 'because they are not suspected about their stains'?
It should have said 'lion-converts'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שֶׁלֹּא נֶחְשְׁדוּ עַל כִּתְמֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rebuilt reading of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 21, where the חכמים rule pure because כותים are lion converts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's written reason (not suspected about stains) does not match the reason this reading needs (lion converts)

steps.title: A new reading: stains from ישראל and כותים are impure, but stains found in Jewish towns are pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rebuilds the משנה a second way. Stains that come from Jews or כותים are impure, since כותים are true converts. Stains found lying in Jewish towns are pure. Jews carefully put away stained clothes, so a stain found lying around must have come from a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: stains from among Jews and from among כותים are impure, because כותים are true converts. Stains found in Jewish towns are pure, because Jews are not suspected about their stains; they definitely put them away.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first reading, the גמרא offers a new one. Here the question is not who owns the stain but where it was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now everyone agrees כותים are true converts, so their stains are impure just like Jewish stains. The 'pure' case is a stain found in a Jewish town. Jews hide their stained clothes, so a stain left in the open must belong to a non-Jew. This fits the משנה's reason, 'they are not suspected about their stains'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means (a new reading of the text)
Those that are found lying around, with no known owner
They definitely put away (hide) them

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
From among Jews and from among Samaritans — impure,
because Samaritans are true converts.
Those found in Jewish towns — pure,
because they are not suspected about their stains,
and they certainly put them away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading from step 21, which step 22 rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new reading of the משנה, based on where the stain was found
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether כותים are true converts
steps.terutzMaskana: כותים are true converts. A stain found in a Jewish town is pure because Jews hide their stains.

steps.title: In the towns of the כותים, רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: The new reading continues. For stains found in towns of the כותים, רבי מאיר says impure, because כותים are suspected of leaving stained clothes around. The חכמים say pure, because they are not suspected, so the stain must be from a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stains found in towns of the כותים: רבי מאיר says impure, because they are suspected about their stains. The חכמים say pure, because they are not suspected about their stains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its new reading of the משנה. It places the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים on stains found lying in towns of the כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is now about how careful the כותים are. רבי מאיר thinks they may leave stained clothes in the open, so a found stain could be theirs and is impure. The חכמים think they hide them just like Jews, so a found stain must be from a non-Jew and is pure. This finally explains the משנה's reason, 'because they are not suspected about their stains'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it impure
Rule it pure
Towns where the כותים live

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: stains that come from Jews or כותים are impure, since כותים are true converts. A stain found in a Jewish town is pure. For a stain found in a town of כותים, רבי מאיר says impure because they are suspected of leaving stains around. The חכמים say pure because they are not suspected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tests a rebuilt משנה. The reading must match the reason the משנה actually gives, not just its ruling.

phrases.aramaic: הַנִּמְצָאִין בְּעָרֵי כּוּתִים — רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא,
phrases.english: Those found in Samaritan towns — Rabbi Meir deems them impure,
because they are suspected about their stains,
and the Sages deem them pure,
because they are not suspected about their stains.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנִּמְצָאִין בְּעָרֵי כּוּתִים — רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the new reading begun in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the dispute on stains found in towns of the כותים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's reason 'not suspected about their stains' seemed not to fit
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is whether כותים are careful to hide their stained clothes; the חכמים say they are, so a found stain is pure

steps.title: Stains found anywhere are pure, with two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that stains found anywhere are pure, except those found in inner rooms or near the בית הטמאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: All stains found anywhere are pure, except those found in the inner rooms or around the house where impure women stayed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a general rule that stains found lying around are pure, and names two places where they are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the idea from step 23: Jews put away stained clothes, so a stain lying in the open probably came from a non-Jew and is pure. Inner rooms are different, because that is where Jews put stained clothes away. The area near the בית הטמאות is also different, because impure women stayed there.

keyTerms.meaning: Inner rooms of the house, where things are put away
The house or room where women stayed while they were נדה
Pure; they do not make anyone impure
Except for

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the stains
that are found in any place are pure,
except for those found in the inner rooms,
and around the house of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' כׇּל הַכְּתָמִים הַנִּמְצָאִים בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. Its logic matches the idea in step 23 that Jews put away stained clothes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stains found lying anywhere are pure, except in inner rooms or near the בית הטמאות.

steps.title: The כותים' house of impurity spreads corpse impurity
steps.stepSummary: The בית הטמאות of the כותים makes things impure through a roof, because they bury stillborn babies there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of impurity of the כותים makes people and things under its roof impure, because they bury stillborn babies there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new rule about the בית הטמאות of the כותים. Being under its roof gives corpse impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stillborn baby is a dead body, and a dead body makes everything under the same roof impure (טומאת אהל). Since the כותים bury stillborns in that house, anyone who enters becomes impure. This is the view of the תנא קמא; רבי יהודה will argue in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes impure through a roof: anything under the same roof as a dead body becomes impure
Stillborn babies or babies who did not live
They bury

phrases.english: The house of impurity of the Samaritans
imparts impurity through a tent,
phrases.notes: This means corpse impurity. Anyone under the same roof as the body becomes impure.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם קוֹבְרִין שָׁם אֶת הַנְּפָלִים.
phrases.english: because they bury the stillborn babies there.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הַטְּמָאוֹת שֶׁל כּוּתִים מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new rule about the בית הטמאות mentioned in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כותים' בית הטמאות transmits corpse impurity through a roof, because stillborns are buried there.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: they threw the stillborns out, they did not bury them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. The כותים did not bury stillborns in the house; they threw them out and an animal dragged them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: they did not bury them there. They threw them out, and an animal would drag the body away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the rule from step 26. He says the house does not give corpse impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about the facts, not the law. Both sides agree a buried stillborn would make the house impure. רבי יהודה says no body stays there, because the babies were thrown out and animals took them away.

keyTerms.meaning: They throw away
Drags it away
A wild animal

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: They would not bury them there,
rather they would throw them out, and an animal would drag it away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the facts behind step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no corpse impurity in the house, because no stillborn stays there.

steps.title: What the כותים are trusted to say
steps.stepSummary: The כותים are trusted to say whether they buried stillborns somewhere, whether an animal gave birth before, and where graves are marked.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are trusted to say 'We buried stillborns there' or 'We did not bury.' They are trusted to say about an animal whether it gave birth before or not. They are trusted about grave markings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists the cases where we believe a כותי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case ties back to step 26: a כותי can tell us whether a place has a buried stillborn. The animal case decides whether its next baby is a בכור, which is holy. They are also believed about which places they marked as graves.

keyTerms.meaning: Trusted; their word is believed
Gave birth for the first time already; this decides whether the next calf is a בכור
Markers set up to show where a grave is

phrases.english: They are trusted to say: 'We buried the stillborns there,'
or 'We did not bury them there,'
they are trusted to say about an animal
whether it has given birth before or has not given birth before,
they are trusted about the marking of graves.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמָנִים לוֹמַר קָבַרְנוּ שָׁם אֶת הַנְּפָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by listing what the כותים are believed about, starting with the burial question from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים are believed about burying stillborns, about a firstborn animal, and about grave markers.

steps.title: What the כותים are not trusted about
steps.stepSummary: The כותים are not trusted about overhanging branches, protruding stones, or a בית הפרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not trusted about overhanging branches, not about stones sticking out of walls, and not about a בית הפרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by listing the cases where we do not believe a כותי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases involve a hidden grave. In the first two, it is unclear which branch or stone hangs over the grave and makes things impure through a roof. A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed up, so bones may be scattered. The next step gives the reason they are not believed here.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches of a tree that hang over the ground
Stones sticking out of a fence or wall
A field where a grave was plowed up, so bones may be scattered. The חכמים treat it as impure.

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules come out of this משנה. Stains found lying in the open are pure, except in inner rooms or near the בית הטמאות. The כותים are believed about some impurity matters (burials, grave markers) and the firstborn animal, but not about overhanging branches, protruding stones, or a בית הפרס.

phrases.english: But they are not trusted about the overhanging branches,
phrases.notes: The worry is that one of these branches hangs over a grave and makes people under it impure.

phrases.english: nor about the protruding stones,
nor about a field where a grave was plowed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of step 28: the cases where the כותים are not believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים are not believed about overhanging branches, protruding stones, or a בית הפרס.

steps.title: The general rule: no trust where they are suspected
steps.stepSummary: The משנה wraps up its two lists with one principle: the כותים are not believed about any matter they are suspected of not keeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: any matter the כותים are suspected about, they are not believed about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is summing up the two lists from the last steps with one clear rule that explains them both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 listed things the כותים are believed about, and step 29 listed things they are not believed about. This rule explains the difference. Where the כותים keep the הלכה themselves, we trust their word. Where they are suspected of ignoring or rejecting a הלכה (like a בית הפרס, or טומאה passed through overhanging branches and protruding stones), their testimony about it means nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule; a summary that covers many cases
Suspected of not keeping a certain הלכה
Believed; trusted as reliable witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: A person is not trusted to testify about a הלכה he himself is suspected of not keeping. This is why the כותים are believed on some טומאה questions but not on others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle goes beyond the כותים. Whether someone is trusted on a matter of הלכה depends on whether he is suspected about that specific matter.

phrases.english: This is the general rule:
any matter that they are suspected about —
they are not believed about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one general principle that explains the cases in steps 28 and 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כותים are not believed about any הלכה they are suspected of not keeping. They are believed only where they keep the הלכה themselves.
